components.label: Page
components.description: The root of every rendered page. It scrolls down; nothing inside it scrolls down by itself.

props.name: title

renders.desktop: A scrolling column beside the sidebar, the title as a heading, content at most 1600 points wide.
renders.phone: A scrolling column under a large title that collapses into the navigation bar; sections 24 points apart, rows bleed to the screen's edges.
renders.tablet: As a phone, with 16-point side margins (the m spacing, as on every form factor but the television).
renders.tv: A full-screen column inside the safe area (60 points top and bottom, 80 at the sides), sections 40 points apart. The title isn't drawn: the top menu says where you are.

components.a11y: Role: main. Label: the title.

components.label: Spotlight
components.description: A large rotating spotlight of a few titles: backdrop, title or logo, a line of facts, a synopsis and buttons.
components.fallbackNote: A Shelf of landscape cards of the same items, titled with the hero's title or "Featured".

props.name: title
props.label: Title
props.help: Named to assistive technology and used by the fallback; not drawn.

props.name: style
props.label: Style
props.help: A full billboard, or a shorter banner.

props.name: autoAdvanceSec
props.label: Seconds per title
props.help: How long each title stays before the next one. 0 never moves by itself.

props.name: showSynopsis
props.label: Show the synopsis
props.help: Two or three lines about the title.

props.name: showLogo
props.label: Use the title's logo
props.help: The title's logo art in place of its name, when it has one.

props.name: actions
props.label: Buttons
props.help: The buttons on each title, in order.

props.name: maxItems
props.label: Most titles
props.help: How many titles it rotates through.

renders.desktop: A 21/9 backdrop at most 620 points tall, text block bottom-left, arrows at the edges on hover, page dots bottom-right.
renders.phone: A 16/9 backdrop the width of the screen (2/3 with style billboard), title and facts over a bottom scrim, buttons below; swipe sideways to change title, page dots under it.
renders.tablet: A 21/9 backdrop with the text block at the bottom-left third.
renders.tv: The top 620 points of the screen: backdrop full width behind a left-to-right scrim, the logo or title at the heading size bottom-left, facts, at most three lines of synopsis, then the buttons in a row. Left and right on the buttons' row past its ends change title; it never advances while one of its buttons has focus.

states.loading: A grey block of the hero's size.

components.a11y: Role: region, labelled by the title prop or "Featured". Each slide is a group labelled "<title>, <facts joined by comma>", announced politely when it changes. With reduced motion it does not advance by itself and cross-fades are cuts.

components.label: Row
components.description: A titled row of cards that scrolls sideways. The workhorse of a home page.

props.name: title

props.help: The heading above the items. Placeholders such as {library} and {each} are filled in.

props.name: subtitle

props.name: cardSize

props.label: Most cards at first

props.label: Message when empty

renders.desktop: A heading with a "See all" link at its end, a row that scrolls by wheel, drag or the arrow buttons that appear at its ends on hover; arrow keys move focus card to card.
renders.phone: A heading with a chevron when there is a See all, then a row that scrolls by touch and bleeds off both edges; cards 12 points apart.
renders.tv: A heading at the title size, then one row of cards 40 points apart that scrolls sideways under focus, the focused card kept a safe-area's width from the left edge and raised with the system's focus effect. states.deferred: Drawn as loading until the client has asked props.more.url, which it does when the section is within one screen of being seen.

states.error: The heading and one line, "Couldn't load this", with a Retry button that asks props.more.url again.
states.loading: Its heading, and as many grey placeholder cards of the card's size as fit, pulsing unless the device asks for reduced motion.

components.a11y: Role: list, labelled by the title. Each card is a list item. When numbered, a card's label starts with "Number <n>".

components.label: Grid
components.description: Cards in rows and columns, as many columns as fit. It pages as the person scrolls: the body of a library.

states.loading: Its heading, and as many grey placeholder cards of the card's size as fit, pulsing unless the device asks for reduced motion.

renders.phone: Picture, then title and subtitle under it in the title and caption sizes. A long press opens the app's own item menu.

components.a11y: Role: button (link on the web). Label: the props its style shows, in the style's order, joined by ", ": progress as "<n> percent watched", watched as "Watched", unwatched as "<n> unwatched", badges as written, a channel as "Channel <number>, <title>, now <now.title>, next <next.title>".

components.fallbackNote: The selected tab's content alone, in a column.

props.name: style

renders.phone: A segmented control (segments) or a scrolling row of text tabs with an underline (tabs); swiping the content sideways changes tab.
renders.tv: A row of pills centred above the content; left and right move between them and the content changes as focus moves; down enters the content.

components.a11y: Role: tablist; each Tab is a tab with selected state; the content is its tabpanel.

components.label: Tab

components.description: The controls that filter and sort a Grid on the same page. The server fills in each filter's choices from what the library holds; a change asks for the page again with the choice as a query parameter. With showCount, the server sends count (a number) and countText, the words to show ("1 title", "12 titles").
components.fallbackNote: Left out: the grid shows everything in its default order.

props.name: target
props.label: Filters

props.name: showCount

props.help: The number of titles found.

renders.desktop: A row of drop-downs with the count at the far end and a Clear button when anything is chosen.
renders.phone: A row of chips that scrolls sideways; a chip opens a bottom sheet of choices. The count sits above it in the caption style.
renders.tv: One row of pills: Sort first, then each filter showing its current choice; OK on a pill opens a full-height list from the right edge to choose from.

components.a11y: Role: toolbar, labelled "Filter and sort". Each field is a pop-up button labelled "<label>: <current choice or Any>".

components.label: Title header
components.description: The top of a title's page: its art, name, facts, score, synopsis and the buttons that play it and act on it. It shows the title the page was opened for. A button that is a toggle (Watch later) has pressed true or false: draw it as on or off and say so to a screen reader; its label and command already match the state.
components.fallbackNote: A column: the backdrop as an Image, the title and overview as Text, and the actions as Buttons in a row.

props.name: layout
props.label: Layout
props.help: Backdrop behind the text, poster beside it, or a compact strip.

renders.desktop: Backdrop behind; poster at the left (layout poster or backdrop), text block beside it, buttons in a row: primary filled, the rest outlined.
renders.phone: Backdrop 16/9 at the top, title and facts under it, a full-width primary button, the other actions as a row of icon buttons with captions, then the synopsis, cut to four lines with More.
renders.tablet: As a phone with the poster beside the text block.
renders.tv: Backdrop across the whole screen under a scrim; the logo or title at the page title size at the left, the facts on one line, at most four lines of synopsis, the buttons in a row with Play first and focused. Sections below scroll up over the backdrop.

states.error: A Notice: "This title isn't available" with a button back to Home.

props.name: style

renders.tv: A row of season pills, then the episodes as a row of episode cards (still, "<n>. <title>", runtime, two lines of synopsis) that scrolls sideways; focus starts on the next episode to watch.
